```{python}
#| label: load-results
import json
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import plotly.express as px
import polars as pl
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import Code, display

metrics = json.loads(Path("metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
run = json.loads(Path("report_metadata.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
# Great Tables accepts HTML in strings; escape values supplied by the run.
display(GT(pl.DataFrame({"Run": [run["title"]]})).fmt(escape, columns="Run"))
```

## Overall performance

Accuracy and macro F1 include failed predictions in their denominators.
Operational coverage is the fraction of records with a resolved prediction.
Mock results test the pipeline and do not measure a real model's quality.

```{python}
display(GT(pl.DataFrame({
    "Metric": ["Support", "Accuracy", "Macro F1", "Operational coverage"],
    "Value": [
        str(metrics["support"]),
        f"{metrics['accuracy']:.3f}",
        f"{metrics['macro_f1']:.3f}",
        f"{metrics['operational_coverage']:.3f}",
    ],
}), rowname_col="Metric"))

for label, key in [("Accuracy", "accuracy_ci95"), ("Macro F1", "macro_f1_ci95")]:
    interval = metrics[key]
    if interval is not None:
        print(f"{label} 95% bootstrap interval: {interval[0]:.3f} to {interval[1]:.3f}")
```

## Language breakdown

```{python}
languages = pl.DataFrame([
    {"Language": language, **values}
    for language, values in metrics["by_language"].items()
])
display(GT(languages, rowname_col="Language")
        .fmt(escape, columns="Language")
        .fmt_number(columns=["accuracy", "macro_f1"], decimals=3))
```

## Class performance

```{python}
classes = pl.DataFrame([
    {"Class": label, **values}
    for label, values in metrics["per_class"].items()
])
display(GT(classes, rowname_col="Class")
        .fmt(escape, columns="Class")
        .fmt_number(columns=["precision", "recall", "f1"], decimals=3))
```

## Confusion matrix

Rows are true labels; columns are predicted labels. Unresolved predictions count
against accuracy and recall but are outside the three displayed prediction columns.

```{python}
#| label: fig-confusion
#| fig-cap: "Counts by true and predicted sentiment."
labels = ["negative", "neutral", "positive"]
matrix = metrics["confusion_matrix"]
fig = px.imshow(
    matrix, x=labels, y=labels, text_auto=True, color_continuous_scale="Blues",
    labels={"x": "Predicted label", "y": "True label", "color": "Records"},
    aspect="auto",
)
fig.update_layout(height=420)
fig.show(renderer="notebook")
```

## Latency and usage

```{python}
print(f"Latency P50/P95: {metrics['latency_p50_ms']:.1f}/{metrics['latency_p95_ms']:.1f} ms")
providers = pl.DataFrame([
    {"Provider": provider, **values}
    for provider, values in metrics["latency_by_provider"].items()
])
display(GT(providers, rowname_col="Provider")
        .fmt(escape, columns="Provider")
        .fmt_number(columns=["p50_ms", "p95_ms"], decimals=1))
display(GT(pl.DataFrame({
    "Metric": ["Input tokens", "Output tokens", "Usage records fraction", "Reported credits"],
    "Value": [str(metrics["usage_input_tokens_total"]), str(metrics["usage_output_tokens_total"]),
              f"{metrics['usage_records_fraction']:.1%}",
              str(metrics["reported_credits_total"]) if metrics["reported_credits_total"] is not None
              else "Unavailable"],
}), rowname_col="Metric"))
```

Token totals sum known usage; a missing usage record does not imply a free request.
Credits are provider-reported units, separate from USD estimates.

## Cost

```{python}
if metrics["cost_usd_total"] is not None:
    print(f"${metrics['cost_usd_total']:.6f} total; "
          f"${metrics['cost_usd_per_1000']:.4f} per 1,000")
else:
    print(f"partial (${metrics['cost_usd_known_total']:.6f} known; "
          f"{metrics['cost_priced_fraction']:.1%} priced)")
```

Partial pricing is not a complete run cost.

## Calibration

Calibration metrics are available only when every prediction has a genuine class
probability vector. Provider-reported confidence is a separate quantity.

```{python}
if metrics["ece"] is None or metrics["brier_score"] is None:
    print("Unavailable: complete class probability vectors were not supplied.")
else:
    print(f"Expected calibration error: {metrics['ece']:.4f}")
    print(f"Multiclass Brier score: {metrics['brier_score']:.4f}")
```

## Run metadata

```{python}
display(Code(json.dumps(run["metadata"], ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), language="json"))
```

These results use synthetic financial feedback with template variations. Exact
deduplication does not establish independence or real-world generalization.
